youtube.description:
Can your landlord demand two years of rent upfront? While Lagos caps advance rent at one year for new tenants and six months for sitting monthly tenants, Cross River sets the strictest rule in Nigeria: individuals cannot be asked for more than three months in advance. Learn the exact statutory provisions in Lagos and Cross River, the 60-day court rule, mandatory receipts, and how to claim your 2026 rent tax relief. Build clean agreements and rent receipts in two minutes at https://docoga.com.ng

General information, not legal advice.

claims.text: In Cross River, a landlord may demand and receive the prescribed rent in advance for a period not exceeding three months from tenants who are individuals, and twelve months from tenants other than individuals.
A landlord in Cross River may lawfully take a year in advance from a company, but only three months from a person.
In Lagos, a landlord cannot demand or receive more than six months advance rent from a sitting monthly tenant.
A sitting yearly tenant in Lagos cannot be asked for more than one year of rent in advance.
For a new or would-be tenant in Lagos, a landlord cannot demand or receive more than one year of rent in advance.
In Lagos, any person who receives or pays rent in excess commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of one hundred thousand naira or three months imprisonment.
Every landlord in Lagos shall issue a receipt on payment of rent.
A landlord in Lagos who fails to issue a rent receipt is liable on conviction to a fine of one hundred thousand naira.
Cross River abolished Rent Tribunals and replaced them with courts where the Governor divides the State into zones and establishes Rent Control Courts.
Under Cross River law, judgment must be delivered not later than two months from the date of service of the hearing notices.
Cross River law applies to all residential accommodation throughout the State except maisonettes.
In computing taxable income from 2026, a rent relief of twenty percent of annual rent paid up to a maximum of five hundred thousand naira is deducted.
